_source_note: 60 glaze recipes from Chapter 11 of Richard Zakin's 'Electric Kiln Ceramics: A Guide to Clays and Glazes' (3rd ed, Krause/F+W Media, 2004) - ingredient/percentage data and Zakin's own surface/color descriptions, condensed rather than quoted verbatim. All recipes in this chapter are written for oxidation firing in an electric kiln, which is why the book exists. Generic material terms (boron frit, soda frit, potash feldspar, red clay, stoneware clay) are Zakin's own category names, not specific branded products - most are left unresolved rather than guessed at, except where this database already defaults a generic term to a standard equivalent (Potash Feldspar -> Custer Feldspar, Soda Feldspar -> Minspar 200, Iron/Iron Oxide -> Red Iron Oxide, Zirconium/Zirconium Opacifier -> Zircopax). Two recipes (Dewitt Mills, Franklin R 92) sum to 88% and 80% respectively as printed in the book - confirmed against the source text, not a transcription gap; kept faithful to the original rather than padded to 100. The Estacada recipe (cone 3) uses 'potash' and 'spodium' in the original where every neighboring recipe spells out 'potash feldspar' and 'spodumene' - treated as the book's own abbreviation/typo and resolved accordingly, noted per-recipe. Surface labels were inferred from Zakin's own prose descriptions and carry surface_source='description'; he states the fired surface for most glazes but not as a separate field. Five have no surface claim in the text and are deliberately left unlabelled rather than guessed.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: Opaque 04 k2
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: A basic opaque low-fire glaze base of boron frit, talc, ball clay, and zirconium opacifier.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: 04 Clear k2
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: A basic transparent low-fire glaze base of boron frit, talc, and ball clay.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: Robin's 1b Clear k2
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: A transparent low-fire glaze base built on spodumene and boron frit 3124, with talc and ball clay.
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.notes: 'boron frit 3124' as printed -> resolved to Frit 3124

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: Mohawk Green F k2
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This recipe is very low in silica and quite high in alumina and in fluxes. Its most significant fluxes are sodium, calcium, boron, and lithium derived respectively from soda spar, boron frit, and lithium carbonate. Its color is a rich saturated green. It has a fairly strong visual texture.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: Millbrook Visitor
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This is a highly durable transparent glaze with a shiny surface.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: Tottman
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This glaze is dry surfaced. Its color is yellow where thick, rust where thin, and it has a good deal of visual texture. It derives its color from the iron in the red clay.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: Cobblestone Base
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This glaze is satin shiny in surface and ivory white in color.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: Lorraine Earth Yellow
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This is a satin shiny glaze. Its color is a soft yellow where thick, tan where thin. Its color is derived from iron in the red clay.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: Wardwell Brown
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This glaze has a satin matte surface. Its color is predominantly brown with persimmon-brown attracting the most notice. It is marked by a tight pattern of ocher spots. It derives its color from iron in the red clay and the stoneware clay.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: Towle Gulf Yellow
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This glaze has a matte surface. Where thick its color is a bright mustard yellow, where thin it's rust red. It derives its color from iron in the red clay.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: 02 Millennium MetalBlack
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This glaze derives its color from the iron and manganese in the Barnard clay and the cobalt oxide addition. Its color is midnight black. Though it has little visual texture, in combination with other glazes it will often encourage strong visual textures.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: 02 Orange Chartreuse
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This glaze has a matte surface. It derives its color from its red clay content. Its color ranges from a chartreuse where thick to a rust where thin.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: 02 Dark Matte
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This glaze has a satin matte surface. It is a red-brown where thin and dark mustard where thick. It derives its color from iron in the red clay.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: Tremaines Persimmon
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This shiny surfaced glaze is cream where thick, and brown where thin. It is low in viscosity and flows away from edges. It derives its color from iron in the stoneware clay and the red clay.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: Millbrook Opaque 2
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This shiny, smooth surfaced glaze is opaque and white in color.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: Millbrook Opaque 3
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This is an opaque, shiny surfaced glaze, white in color.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: Cadwells Base
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: The surface of this glaze is a dry matte. It is opaque and its color is a muted bluish green.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: Dewitt Mills
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This glaze is opaque and its surface is satin matte. Its color varies from cream to tan (a thick application encourages a cream color). It has a good “hand” and is marked by strong visual texture.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: Dewitt White 1
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This is an opaque, soft, satin matte glaze. Its color is ivory white. Its slightly grayed color is derived from its stoneware clay content.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: Fulton 4a Deep Blue
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This opaque glaze has a soft looking waxy matte surface. Where thinly applied it is gray, where thick it is deep slate blue. Its high strontium content may encourage sedimenting.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: Oz Strontium IV
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This opaque glaze has a velvety matte surface. Its color is a strong green. Its surface is similar to a high barium glaze but doesn't have the toxicity of barium. It derives these characteristics from its high strontium content, which may cause it to sediment.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: Richmond Mills
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This glaze is opaque and has a satin matte surface. Its color is a soft cream where thick and is a light amber where thin. It is durable and would be an excellent liner glaze.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: Snyders 2
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This glaze is opaque and its surface is satin shiny. Its color ranges from silver-gray to ocher and it is marked by visual texture. It derives its color from the iron in iron oxide and in the stoneware clay. It is quite durable.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: Sodus Point 2
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This glaze is opaque and matte surfaced. Its color ranges from yellow-ocher to brown. It derives its color from its Barnard/stoneware clay content.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: Orwell Amber
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This glaze has a satin surface. Its color is butterscotch where thick, and amber-brown where thin. It takes its color from iron in the red and stoneware clays and from the titanium in the stoneware clay.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: Wardwell Persimmon
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This glaze has a stony satin matte surface. Its color is a soft persimmon-brown. It takes its color mainly from the iron in the stoneware clay and the red clay.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: Dutcherville Barn Red
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This glaze has a satin shiny surface. It is a bright iron red in color. Iron in the red clay gives this glaze its vibrant color.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: Minoa Amber
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This glaze has a satin shiny surface. The glaze is tan where thick and red-amber where thin. The color is derived from iron in the red clay and the stoneware clay. Color and surface are significantly enhanced by the presence of tin oxide.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: Fairdale Bridge
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This glaze has a satin matte surface. Its color is a very light yellow. The rutile in this recipe acts as both a flux and a colorant.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: Dewitt Dark Tan 3
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This rich satin matte surface varies in color and texture. It will produce various browns, and has a mottled appearance. This glaze takes its color from the iron and manganese in the Barnard clay.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: Stone Hill
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This glaze has a satin surface. It is a creamy tan in color. Visual texture results from variations in the glaze thickness. This glaze takes its color from the iron in the red clay.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: Checkered House Ocher
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This glaze has a matte surface. It is a soft, earth yellow in color. This glaze takes its color from the iron in the rutile and the stoneware clay.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: Howardville
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This glaze has a satin matte surface. It is earth yellow where applied thickly and amber where thin. Color is derived from the iron in the red and stoneware clays. Strong variations in the texture will result from differing glaze thicknesses.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: Bethel Gray
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This glaze has a durable satin matte surface. It is gray-mustard where thick and orange-brown where thin. Some dark brown speckles may appear on the gray-mustard ground. It takes its color from the iron and titanium in the red and stoneware clays.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: Canton Brown
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This glaze has a satin matte surface. Its color varies from ocher to brown. Its color is derived from the iron in the red clay and the cobalt colorant.
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.notes: 1.5% cobalt carbonate - ocher and brown; 2.5% cobalt - rich matte black

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: Estacada
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: Estacada will produce a matte glaze of warm yellow where used thickly and orange-tan where thin. It has some light speckling and an earthy appearance. Color is derived from iron in the red and stoneware clays.
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.notes: 'potash' as printed -> resolved to Potash Feldspar; 'spodium' as printed -> resolved to Spodumene

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: C/3 Millennium MetalBlack
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This glaze has a metallic grainy surface with a strong shine. Its color is an ebony black. Color is derived from iron and manganese in the Barnard clay. With the addition of 1% cobalt oxide its color is midnight black. Though it has little visual texture when used alone, in combination with other glazes it will often encourage strong visual textures.
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.notes: 'boron frit (3124)' as printed -> resolved to Frit 3124

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: Denton
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This glaze is opaque and has a satin shiny surface. Its color is a cool green.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: Soft Tan Base
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This glaze is opaque and has a matte surface. It is a warm ivory in color.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: Satin White
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This is an opaque glaze with a satin matte surface. Its color is a silvery white.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: Transparent Matte Glaze
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This glaze has a satin matte surface. It is translucent. This is a very unusual recipe in that it is a translucent matte glaze. This interesting and useful glaze type was popular in the United States from the early 1900s to the 1930s.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: MetalBlack
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This glaze has a satin matte surface. Its color is a metallic black. It derives its color from its high percentage of Barnard clay along with the copper colorant.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: Corinth Corners
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This is a shiny opaque glaze. Its color is a deep gray-mustard with tinges of rust at the edges of the form where the glaze is thin. It derives its color from iron in the very high percentage of red clay.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: Estacada 18
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This glaze has a satin matte surface. It is a bleached mustard color where thin and amber-brown where thick. Color is derived from the iron in the red clay.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: Estacada Gray-Ocher
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This glaze has a shiny surface. Where thick its color is a soft cream, where thin the color is a light burnt orange. Color is derived from iron in the red clay.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: Estacada Orange-Ocher
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This glaze has a shiny surface. Where thick this glaze is a soft cream and where thin it takes on a burnt orange color. Visual textures may result from variations in the glaze thickness. Color is derived from the iron in the red clay.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: Barnard Estacada
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This glaze has a shiny surface. Its color is a deep red umber. It may flow away from edges where thin. The source of its color is in its iron and manganese content from the Barnard clay.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: Maple View Cream-Orange
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This glaze has a satin matte surface. It is orange where thick and a light cream-orange where thin. Visual texture may result from variations in glaze thickness. Its color is derived from the iron in the red clay.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: Sayles Corners
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This glaze has a satin matte surface. Its color varies from light mustard if applied thickly to a light orange if thin. The source of color is the iron in the red clay.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: Crawling Vitgobe
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This vitreous engobe has a complex surface that is marked by both bubbling and wrinkling. Its color is a cream-tan. Both its color and complex texture are derived from its high percentage of stoneware clay.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: Mullen Hill Base
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This glaze has a smooth eggshell matte surface. Its color is an oyster white. With the addition of 2% copper carbonate its color ranges from amber to brown to green.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: Vans White
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This glaze has a satin shiny surface. Its color is white.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: Ridgebury
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This glaze has a satin shiny surface. It is transparent and its color ranges from iron green to orange.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: Franklin R 92
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This glaze has a satin surface. Its color ranges from red-brown to burnt umber. It is marked with strong visual texture derived from calcium and magnesium.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: Gateville R 92
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This translucent glaze has a satin surface. Its color ranges from ocher to amber to dark brown. It is marked by a strong visual texture derived from lithium, calcium/magnesium, and titanium.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: H GK 92
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: The surface of this opaque glaze ranges from stony/dry to pitted. Its color is bone-white.
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.notes: 'zirconium' as printed -> resolved to Zirconium Opacifier

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: Harpersfield R 92
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This opaque glaze has a satin surface. Its color is a red-brown. It is unstable and bubbling when used in a thick application.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: Deerpark Base
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This glaze has a satin matte surface. Its color ranges from an amber-cream to amber. It is marked by strong textures derived from iron and calcium/magnesium.

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: Pilgrim Vitreous Engobe 92
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This opaque glaze is semi-vitreous with a slight sheen. It is white in color.
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.notes: 'zirconium' as printed -> resolved to Zirconium Opacifier

zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.name: Woodbourne Base 92
zakin_electric_kiln_glazes.description: This opaque glaze has a satin matte surface. Its color is an amber-yellow.
